3	## Document Overview: Core Case + Supporting Retellings
4	
5	The milk-testing dispute case (1889–1925) from Segment 1 continues across multiple retellings:

12	## Cast of Characters and Relationships
13	*(Carried from Segment 2 with additions)*
14	
15	**Ansel Keddie** (Tester, Ostrey Hollow station, 1896–1924)
16	- Ran the skimming station 7 miles up valley from Larrow Green
17	- Kept meticulous test books in his own hand, handwriting "like print," no blots across 29 seasons
18	- Married to Orra Keddie
19	- Denies taking cream: "I have never taken a pound of cream out of that station and there is not a man in this room who thinks I have when he is by himself" (March 1925 statement)
20	- Put out (fired) April 30, 1925, after arbitration award
21	- Died in the 1930s, still under stigma from the 1919 letter
22	- His question mark in the test book about the 1911 anomaly stood unanswered for 14 years
23	- EXONERATED in 1958 (35 years after dismissal, 24 years after death) by scientific analysis
24	
25	**Ivy Keddie** (Granddaughter, historian)
26	- Ansel's granddaughter; Duncan Keddie was her father (teacher at Ashlin)
27	- In 1959, presented findings to Ordell County Historical Society at Ashlin
28	- Conducted scientific forensic analysis of condemned pipettes from 1923
29	- Used calibrated burette to measure nine unbroken pipettes from station crate
30	- Measured pipettes delivering 16.72 cc instead of 17.6 cc (95% of correct volume)
31	- Published findings in Bulletin No. 471 with Professor Vaught
32	
33	**Wilbur Teague** (Bookkeeper, 1905–1945)
34	- Kept the Association's books from 1905 to 1945 (40 years)
35	- Invented the "station-gain" account in 1905 to track difference between credited vs. received butterfat
36	- Station-gain line ran at 5.25 percent of actual cream, year after year
37	- Noted in books: "Ostrey Hollow: butter fat credited to patrons on station test, 57,760 lb. Butter fat received at Larrow Green in station cream, 60,800 lb. Station gain, 3,040 lb, five and a quarter per cent, as usual. Carried to the general account."
38	- Warned Selby Vose about the account in 1916; was told to "let it alone"
39	- Testified at 1925 board of arbitration hearing
40	- Wrote memoir "The Books of the Association" in 1948, three years after retiring
41	- Emphasized: "One man weighed the milk, one man drew the sample, one man made the test, one man wrote the figure... one man ran the separator... no second man in that building from the spring to the fall"
42	- Noted Selby Vose signed the annual sheets every year without comment
43	
44	**Orra Keddie** (Ansel's wife)
45	- First cousin of old Mrs. Vose
46	- Sister of Emmet Brant (largest milk patron)
47	- After 1919 letter, rift with her brother Emmet: "they did not speak. Not one word"
48	- Would walk to Larrow Green rather than pass her brother's lane
49	- Outlived Ansel and suffered the stigma for years after his death
50	
51	**Emmet Brant** (Farmer, Hessel Bottom)
52	- Largest milk patron to Ostrey Hollow station
53	- Brother of Orra Keddie; brother-in-law of Ansel
54	- Stopped speaking to Ansel Keddie after 1919
55	
56	**Gideon Vose** (Association founder and president)
57	- Started the Larrow Valley Cooperative Creamery Association in 1889
58	- First president, held office 22 years until 1911
59	- Died in 1917
60	
61	**Selby Vose** (Association manager, 1913–1938)
62	- Son of Gideon Vose
63	- Became manager in 1913
64	- Signed the 1919 circular letter
65	- Signed all annual sheets; Teague brought them to him each spring
